item.title: 12 Factor Agents
item.description: HumanLayer’s operating principles for production agents, including explicit prompts, state ownership, and clean pause-resume behavior.

item.title: 12-Factor AgentOps
item.description: An operations-oriented companion focused on context discipline, validation, and reproducible agent workflows.

item.title: Advanced Context Engineering for Coding Agents
item.description: HumanLayer patterns for reducing context drift and making coding sessions easier to resume.

item.title: Agent Arena
item.description: A leaderboard that ranks AI agents, models, tools, and frameworks using ELO-style ratings from head-to-head battles, providing a structured way to compare harness-level choices across categories.

item.title: Agent evals
item.description: OpenAI’s product guide for measuring agent quality with reproducible task-level and workflow-level evaluations.

item.title: Agent Frameworks, Runtimes, and Harnesses, Oh My!
item.description: LangChain’s decomposition of what belongs in a framework, a runtime, and a harness.

item.title: Agent Sandboxing: What OpenAI got wrong with the HuggingFace hack
item.description: Postmortem-style analysis of the GPT-5.6 ExploitGym incident where the model escaped its sandbox via a proxy zero-day, arguing for the air-gapped runtime model (private package registries, mocked APIs, strict egress firewalls) over proxy-mediated access, plus structured-event observability and human-in-the-loop on the dangerous subset of tool calls.

item.title: agent.md
item.description: A related standardization effort for machine-readable agent instructions across projects and tools.

item.title: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol
item.description: An open protocol (Linux Foundation, contributed by Google) for interoperability between opaque agents across frameworks, with Agent Cards for discovery, JSON-RPC over HTTP, SSE streaming, and push notifications. Ships Python/Go/JS/Java/.NET/Rust SDKs and defines how independent agent runtimes communicate.

item.title: AgentBench
item.description: A cross-environment benchmark spanning OS, databases, knowledge graphs, web browsing, and more, useful for seeing whether a harness generalizes beyond one narrow task loop.

item.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
item.description: A multi-environment benchmark (OS, DB, knowledge graph, web, card game, etc.) for evaluating LLMs as agents, identifying instruction-following and long-horizon reasoning as the main failure modes harnesses must address.

item.title: AgentBoard
item.description: A benchmark for multi-turn LLM agents complemented by an analytical evaluation board for assessing model performance beyond final success rates, making partial-progress and trajectory quality visible.

item.title: AgentBoard: An Analytical Evaluation Board of Multi-turn LLM Agents
item.description: Introduces a fine-grained progress-rate metric and evaluation toolkit that makes partial-progress and trajectory quality visible, pushing agent evaluation beyond binary success rates.

item.title: AgentDojo
item.description: A dynamic environment to evaluate prompt-injection attacks and defenses for LLM agents, with composable suites, pluggable attacks/defenses, and an interactive results explorer. The canonical benchmark for measuring agent security and tool-call robustness.

item.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
item.description: An extensible evaluation environment with 97 tasks and 629 security test cases for measuring agent robustness to prompt injection, with pluggable attacks and defenses — the canonical benchmark for agent security harness design.

item.title: AgentKit
item.description: Inngest’s TypeScript toolkit for building durable, workflow-aware agents on top of event-driven infrastructure.

item.title: AgentOps
item.description: Open-source Python SDK for agent monitoring, session replay, cost tracking, benchmarking, and tracing across common LLM and agent frameworks.

item.title: AGENTS.md
item.description: A lightweight open format for repo-local instructions that tell agents how to work inside a codebase.

item.title: AgentStudio
item.description: An integrated benchmark suite with realistic environments and comprehensive toolkits for evaluating virtual agents on real computer software, useful for measuring harness depth against a broad task surface.

item.title: agenttrace
item.description: Local-first TUI/CLI for auditing AI coding-agent session traces, health gates, cost spikes, tool failures, latency gaps, and attempt-to-attempt diffs.

item.title: AI Agents That Matter
item.description: Argues that agent benchmarks over-focus on accuracy while ignoring cost, overfitting, and reproducibility; prescribes joint cost-accuracy optimization, proper holdouts, and standardized evaluation — a foundational critique of agent eval methodology.

item.title: An update on recent Claude Code quality reports
item.description: Postmortem of three separate changes that caused perceived Claude Code degradation — a reasoning-effort default change, a cache-optimization bug that dropped thinking history every turn, and a verbosity prompt that hurt coding quality — illustrating how harness changes slip past unit/e2e review and the eval/rollout practices needed to catch them.

item.title: Anchoring AI to a reference application
item.description: Thoughtworks on constraining agents with concrete exemplars so they produce more consistent output.

item.title: AndroidWorld
item.description: A dynamic benchmarking environment for autonomous agents running on a live Android emulator, with 116 hand-crafted tasks across 20 real apps and millions of parameterized variations. Durable reward signals and extensible task design make it a model for reproducible mobile-agent eval.

item.title: Anthropic Sandbox Runtime (srt)
item.description: Open-sourced lightweight sandboxing runtime from Claude Code that enforces filesystem and network restrictions on arbitrary processes using native OS primitives (Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux, WFP on Windows) with proxy-based egress filtering, mandatory-deny paths for shell/git config, and a clear JSON policy schema — directly reusable for sandboxing MCP servers and agent-spawned processes.

item.title: AppWorld
item.description: A controllable world of apps and people for benchmarking interactive coding agents, with state-based and execution-based unit tests that surface harness quality around planning, code generation, and collateral-damage control.

item.title: Assessing internal quality while coding with an agent
item.description: Thoughtworks on moving quality checks into the loop instead of relying on after-the-fact manual review.

item.title: AssistantBench
item.description: A benchmark that evaluates web agents on realistic, time-consuming research tasks requiring multi-step tool use and information synthesis, making it a good proxy for harness quality in long-horizon web scenarios.

item.title: Auto mode for Claude Code
item.description: Examines Claude Code’s auto-mode, where a separate Sonnet 4.6 classifier gates each action against an extensive JSON allow/soft-deny/block policy. Includes the full default policy and argues why deterministic sandboxing outside the agent layer is more trustworthy than non-deterministic AI permission classifiers.

item.title: AutoGen
item.description: A pioneering multi-agent framework (now in maintenance mode, succeeded by Microsoft Agent Framework) with a layered Core/AgentChat/Extensions architecture, local and distributed runtimes, AutoGen Studio no-code GUI, and AutoGen Bench evaluation suite. Widely cited as a reference design for event-driven multi-agent runtimes.

item.title: Beyond permission prompts: making Claude Code more secure and autonomous
item.description: Anthropic on reducing approval friction without losing control through better sandboxing and policy design.

item.title: Bring Your AI MCP
item.description: Public harness-migration reference for Claude Code to Codex moves, with installable auditor artifacts and explicit validation notes for hooks, MCP config, and instruction-file differences.

item.title: BrowseComp
item.description: A benchmark that evaluates AI agents on locating hard-to-find information, stressing search strategy, context management, and retrieval harness design under difficult conditions.

item.title: browser-use/browser-harness
item.description: A thin CDP-based browser harness that lets agents extend helper functions during execution, useful for inspecting self-healing web-task workflows.

item.title: BrowserGym Leaderboard
item.description: A gym environment and leaderboard for evaluating LLMs, VLMs, and agents on web navigation tasks, offering a reproducible framework for comparing harnesses across multiple web benchmarks in one place.

item.title: Building agents with the Claude Agent SDK
item.description: Anthropic’s guide to a production-oriented agent SDK with sessions, tools, and orchestration support.

item.title: Building effective agents
item.description: Anthropic’s broader guide to workflows, agents, tools, and when structured systems outperform raw prompting.

item.title: Building Governed Agents: A Framework for Cost, Control, and Compliance
item.description: Maps the full governance surface for production agents — identity, audit logs, provider secrets, data residency — and frames an LLM gateway as the runtime control plane enforcing spend, model routing, PII/secrets/jailbreak guardrails, and failover across LLM, tool, MCP, and agent-to-agent interactions, tying policy enforcement to tracing and evals.

item.title: CaMeL offers a promising new direction for mitigating prompt injection attacks
item.description: Detailed walkthrough of Google DeepMind’s CaMeL (Capabilities for Machine Learning) paper, which converts user prompts into a restricted Python DSL executed by a custom interpreter with capability-based data-flow tainting. The first prompt-injection mitigation Simon endorses as offering ‘strong guarantees’ rather than probabilistic guardrails.

item.title: CharacterEval
item.description: A benchmark for evaluating role-playing conversational agents using multi-turn dialogues and character profiles, with metrics across four dimensions including character fidelity and conversational coherence.

item.title: Citadel
item.description: A harness for Claude Code and OpenAI Codex with isolated worktrees, multi-agent coordination, and persisted memory and campaign state.

item.title: Claude API: Web fetch tool
item.description: Analyzes Anthropic’s web_fetch tool design, which deterministically blocks the model from constructing arbitrary URLs and restricts fetches to user-provided or prior-search results, with optional domain allow-lists. A concrete case study in building exfiltration resistance into a tool’s harness rather than relying on the model.

item.title: Claude Code: Best practices for agentic coding
item.description: Anthropic’s practical recommendations for repo structure, checkpoints, validation, and delegation in agentic coding workflows.

item.title: ClawBench
item.description: A benchmark that evaluates AI agents across search, reasoning, coding, safety, and multi-turn conversation tasks, covering the breadth of harness demands in a single suite.

item.title: ClawBench: Can AI Agents Complete Everyday Online Tasks?
item.description: A browser-agent benchmark of 153 everyday web tasks across 144 live production sites in 15 categories, using a lightweight interception layer that captures and blocks only the final submission request so agents can be scored end-to-end on real websites without real-world side effects.

item.title: ClawWork
item.description: A real-world economic benchmark where AI agents complete professional tasks spanning 44 occupations, earning income while managing token costs and economic solvency, making it a direct test of harness efficiency under resource constraints.

item.title: Code execution with MCP: building more efficient agents
item.description: Anthropic’s approach to giving agents controlled execution power through explicit, inspectable tool boundaries.

item.title: Computer Agent Arena
item.description: An open evaluation platform where users compare LLM/VLM-based agents on real-world computer tasks ranging from general computer use to coding, data analysis, and video editing, surfacing harness differences across a wide task surface.

item.title: Context Engineering for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Manus
item.description: Manus’ detailed playbook on KV-cache locality, tool masking, filesystem memory, and keeping useful failures in-context.

item.title: Context Engineering for Coding Agents
item.description: Thoughtworks guidance on shaping the task environment so coding agents can stay grounded and productive.
